title: Escalate alerts by deterministic once, repeated, and persistent rules
narrative: Models may suggest what to do about an alert, but fixed rules decide how far it escalates. A one-off alert is only logged, an alert that keeps coming back is shown to the operator, and one that persists proposes a repair. Thresholds can be tuned per alert, the same count always gives the same answer, and nonsensical thresholds are refused. Decision-plane policy already separates model proposal from code decision (`fangore_decision_plane_policy`). Tracks MH-PA-06[^insp-pa-06].
implementation: `AlertEscalationPolicy.evaluate(alert_id, occurrence_count)` in `alert_escalation.py` maps counts to the `AlertStage` literal (`log` → `surface` → `propose`) from default thresholds and optional per-alert overrides; thresholds must be ordered. `AlertOccurrenceCounter` is an in-memory reference counter that feeds the policy. No model participates. Complements `JudgementPolicy` / decision-plane verdicts; hosts own durable alert counts.
validation: Harness `cli` scenario `alert_escalation_stages.yaml`. Hard expects on declared observation keys.
